children: By Emmanuel Bruce and Christian Akorlie
Ghana's consumer inflation rose to 5.0% year-on-year in August, from 4.6% in July, the statistics service said on Wednesday.
Government statistician Alhassan Iddrisu said housing, water and energy were the biggest drivers of inflation, accounting for 29.4% of the overall rate, followed by food and beverages at 29.1%.
"Overall, inflation has declined by more than half in 12 months, and on month-to-month basis, prices decreased 1% in August, the sharpest monthly fall of the year so far," Iddrisu said.
The gold-, oil- and cocoa-producing nation has been emerging from its most severe economic crisis in decades.
Consumer inflation stood at 11.5% in August last year.
Ghana's finance ministry reaffirmed its key macroeconomic targets in a mid-year budget review in July, citing stronger-than-expected economic performance in the first half of the year.

The central bank left its main interest rate unchanged for a second consecutive meeting in July, citing renewed conflict in the Middle East as a key risk and stressing the need for vigilance to keep inflation within its 6%–10% target range.

In July, the IMF completed the final review of Ghana's $3 billion support program, unlocking about $371 million in funding. The Fund said Ghana's debt restructuring was largely complete and its debt-servicing risk had eased to moderate, but warned that continued reforms and tight fiscal discipline were needed to address remaining vulnerabilities.
